text: The method constructs proxy labels Ỹᵢ = Yᵢ·𝟙{Uᵢ≥û} + Ŷᵢ·𝟙{Uᵢ<û} by collecting expert labels only where model uncertainty Uᵢ exceeds a calibrated threshold û, guaranteeing average labeling error ≤ ε with probability ≥ 1-α (Theorem 2.1).
Uncertainty calibration is performed via a multicalibration algorithm that adjusts per-example uncertainty estimates across feature/demographic subgroups (Section 2.1).
A PAC router extends the method to route among k candidate models using a learned weighting function w_θ optimized via implicit gradients with a sigmoid relaxation for differentiability (Section 3).

At an error tolerance of ε=0.05, the single-model method yields 14-28% expert-labeling budget savings on text tasks with GPT-4o, 39-60% savings on image tasks with ResNet-152, and 16-51% savings on continuous-label tasks.
Multi-model routing between GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 yields 42% budget savings, and up to 482% relative cost savings in a cost-sensitive setting incorporating per-source and expert labeling costs.
